blocks.text: General Management of Trauma and Injuries

Trauma may occur because of motor vehicle crashes, fights, falls, gunshots, sports, animal bites etc. and is associated with head, musculoskeletal, visceral, and neurovascular injuries. The aim of managing trauma is to prevent further injuries and life- threatening complications that may lead to increased morbidity and mortality. There is a systematic trauma protocol in place, ABCDE protocol, emphasizing on the primary survey, resuscitation, secondary survey, and finally definitive care.

blocks.text: TBI is defined as an alteration in brain function, or other evidence of brain pathology, caused by an external force. TBI is a leading cause of death and permanent disability worldwide. Primary brain injury occurs at time of trauma (e.g., cortical contusions, brain lacerations, diffuse axonal injury) while secondary injury develops following the initial insult (brain edema, hypoxemia, ischemia due to elevated intracranial pressure). TBI is often associated with ophthalmic, ENT, dental and maxillofacial injuries.

Acute spinal cord injury (SCI) refers to disturbances to patients normal sensory, motor, or autonomic function resulting from trauma. Following the initial insult, up to 25% of spinal cord injuries is thought to occur not at the time of the initial trauma but later during treatment or transport. SCI management, therefore, should be multidisciplinary incorporating appropriate prehospital services, Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) protocols, prompt neurosurgical interventions, and timely rehabilitation.
